Prevention: Plough soil 2-3 times before planting to control weeds which could be host to thrips
Monitoring: Regular scouting 3 times/week for first 30 days after transplanting
To monitor, wet hand with water and brush hand across top of plant to see if thrips stick to hand.
If there are 10-20 thrips on your hand then use
Feeding damage caused by thrips causes leaf curling and discoloration.
Monitor natural enemies (e.g. ladybeetle, dragonflies, spider, waterbug, Predatory thrips, coccinellid beetles, anthocorid bugs, and staphylinid beetles)
Direct Control: Flood rice field for 1-2 days if population is high
If rice field has no water, use nets or scarf to collect adults
Nitrogen fertilizer (0.2 kg/m2) to improve tiller growth
Restrictions: Spray in morning between 6-10 am or in afternoon between 3-6 pm
Killing natural enemies could lead to outbreaks of secondary pests
Note: - for all pesticides usage to follow instructions on product label
Dinotefuran; apply at the rate of 1L/ha in the morning or evening.
